title: McPhearson's Farewell
transcription:
McPhearson's Farewell

Farewell ye dungeons dark and strong,
farewell, farewell to thee.
McPhearson's time will may be lang
on yonder gallows tree.

Chorus:
Say wantonly, say wantonly,
say dauntingly gaed he
For he played a tune as he dance
around below the gallows tree.

Little did me mither think
when she did cradle me,
That I would turn a roving boy
and die on yonder tree.

Chorus

For it's by a woman's treacherous hand
that I'm condemned to die.
Below the ledge o'er the window she stood,
a blanket she threw o'er me.

Chorus

Well some come here to see me hung,
and some to buy my fiddle.
Before I would part with her
I'd break her through the middle.

Chorus

I took my fiddle in both my hands
and broke her o'er a stone.
There's none that shall play on thee
when I am dead and gone.

Chorus

When his reprieve was coming o'er
to set McPhearson free
They put the clock a quarter fore
and hung him to a tree.

Chorus

Farewell ye dungeons dark and strong,
farewell, farewell to thee.
McPhearson's time will may be lang
on yonder gallows tree.

Chorus
